cards.text: Meet Noah, friend: a righteous man, blameless in his generation, who walked with God. He has three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth.
Now the rest of the earth? Whew. God looks it over and sees it's corrupt, because all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.

cards.question: Besides being corrupt in the sight of God, what is the earth full of?

cards.text: Then God speaks to Noah, and it's heavy: "The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence."

cards.question: God tells Noah He will destroy the living creatures but leave the earth itself standing.
Destruction is coming, but God has a plan for Noah. What does God tell Noah to make for himself?

cards.text: Then God hands Noah the building plans: gopher wood, rooms, pitch inside and out, a roof, a door in the side, three decks, and 300 cubits long. Friend, I needed three tries to put together one cookie shelf, and it came with PICTURES.

cards.question: Noah has his orders to build an ark. God says He will bring ___ upon the earth.
God says everything on the earth will perish in the flood.

cards.text: And then comes the best word in God's whole speech to Noah. "But."

cards.question: Everything on the earth will perish. But what does God say He will establish with Noah?
God tells Noah he will enter the ark. Who goes in with him?

answers.text: His wife and sons and their wives
His father Lamech and his brothers
His sons and all their servants

cards.text: Then God gets to the animals. Not visiting, friend. MOVING IN.

cards.question: God tells Noah to bring ___ of every living creature into the ark, male and female.
God says every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to Noah.

cards.text: One more thing on the list: every kind of food that is eaten, gathered for Noah's family and the animals. I stress out over packing ONE cookie box, and God just handed this man a shopping list for a whole boat.

cards.question: Noah has the plans, the animal list and the food list from God. How much of it does Noah do?

answers.text: Most of it with a few changes
Just the ark and nothing more

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Noah it's go time: "Go into the ark, you and all your family". And He tells Noah why.

cards.question: The LORD tells Noah to take his family into the ark. What reason does He give?

cards.text: Now God gets specific about the animals: the clean ones, the unclean ones and the birds of the air. Friend, that is a LOT of math for one man.

cards.question: How many pairs of every kind of clean animal does Noah take with him?
For every kind of unclean animal, Noah takes just one pair, a male and its mate.

cards.text: Then God gives Noah the timeline. Seven days from now, He will send rain on the earth.

cards.question: Once God sends the rain on the earth, how long will it fall?

cards.text: Noah does all that the LORD commanded, and he's 600 years old when the floodwaters come. Six HUNDRED, friend, and I got a little worn around the edges and ended up in a junk drawer.
Noah's family heads into the ark to escape the flood. And the animals come to Noah two by two, male and female, as God had commanded.

cards.question: Noah's sons go into the ark, but their wives stay behind.

cards.text: Seven days pass, and the floodwaters come, right when God said they would. It's the seventeenth day of the second month, in the six hundredth year of Noah's life.

cards.question: The flood starts on the seventeenth day of the second month. Where does all that water come from?

answers.text: The great deep and the heavens
The Jordan and the Salt Sea

cards.text: The rain falls for forty days and forty nights, and every kind of creature is inside the ark with Noah's family. And I thought keeping six cookie cutters in line on one counter was a JOB.

cards.question: Every creature is inside the ark, as God commanded Noah. Who shuts Noah in?

cards.text: The door is shut. For forty days the flood keeps coming on the earth, and the waters rise.

cards.question: As the floodwaters rise, what happens to the ark?

answers.text: It is lifted high above the earth
It gets stuck deep in the mud
It is broken apart by the waves

cards.text: The waters keep surging and rising, and the ark floats on the surface. Friend, I PANIC when the rinse water in my mixing bowl gets close to the top.

cards.question: Finally, the waters completely prevail upon the earth. How far up do they reach?

answers.text: Up to the tops of the trees

cards.question: The high mountains are covered. The water rises over the mountaintops to a depth of ___ cubits.

cards.text: Then comes the hard part, friend. Every living thing that moved upon the earth perished: birds, livestock, animals, every swarming creature and all mankind.

cards.question: Every living thing on the face of the earth is blotted out. Only Noah and those with him in the ark remain.

cards.text: And the waters prevail upon the earth for 150 days. We'll leave the ark right there on the water for now, but stick around, friend, because this story is NOT finished.

findings.problem: The joke uses two images. It starts with packing one cookie box, then switches to God handing Noah a shopping list for a whole boat. That second image mixes a modern errand into the Bible setting.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 9 says right before this that "Noah's family heads into the ark." That already answers whether the sons' wives go in. Stop 1 card 12 also asked about the same fact from 6:18, so this question has no challenge left.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 5 of the 7 choice cards (2, 4, 7, 12, 14). There are 2 true or false cards and no fill in the blank cards, so one type dominates this stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card opens with "The door is shut," which retells Genesis 7:16 ("Then the LORD shut him in"). It cites only Genesis 7:17, so the citation should be Genesis 7:16-17.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The blank is the exact depth of the water (fifteen cubits). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason toward fifteen rather than fifty or thirty, so it is a pure luck guess at a detail they haven't seen. This is like the Psalm 23 oil example that the docs mark as bad. The detail is also not needed to understand the passage.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
